title: Shared Shifts
statement: Two team rosters list employee IDs in non-decreasing order, and an ID can appear more than once in a roster.
Return the IDs that appear in both rosters, in increasing order, each listed once.
constraints: a and b are sorted in non-decreasing order

hints: A hash set works, but it ignores that both lists are already sorted. How could you use that?
Walk both lists at once with one index each, always moving the index that points at the smaller value.
When the values match, record it unless it equals the last value you recorded, then move both indices.
pitfalls: Listing an ID more than once when it repeats in both rosters.
Not moving either index on a match, which loops forever.
Checking for duplicates against the wrong previous value.
Using a set and losing the O(1) extra space the sorted order allows.
interviewerNotes: Ask them to compare the hash set and two-pointer approaches and when each is better.
Follow-up: one roster has 10 IDs and the other has 10 million. Strong answers binary search the big one for O(m log n).
